excerpt: Timescale, now called Tiger Data, makes TimescaleDB, the open-source time-series extension for PostgreSQL, and the managed Tiger Cloud. Valued at over $1B after a $110M Series C led by Tiger Global.
content:
Timescale is the company behind TimescaleDB, an open-source extension that turns PostgreSQL into a database for time-series data: metrics, sensor readings, prices, events and other data that arrives with a timestamp. You keep using ordinary SQL and the Postgres ecosystem, while TimescaleDB adds automatic partitioning by time, compression and fast aggregation over large volumes. The company also runs Tiger Cloud, a managed PostgreSQL service, and sells TimescaleDB Enterprise for self-managed, on-premises and edge deployments.

Renamed Tiger Data. In 2025 the company changed its name from Timescale to Tiger Data. In a post announcing the change, co-founders Ajay Kulkarni and Mike Freedman said the company had grown beyond a time-series database and wanted to build a faster PostgreSQL for modern analytical and agentic workloads; the open-source extension keeps the TimescaleDB name, and the tiger had been the company's mascot since 2017. The legal entity remains Timescale, Inc., doing business as Tiger Data, and timescale.com now redirects to tigerdata.com.

Its About page says the founders started in 2015 by building an IoT platform and then built TimescaleDB so Postgres could handle machine data at scale. Kulkarni is founder and CEO, and Freedman is founder and CTO. In its Series C announcement the company said it had raised $110 million led by Tiger Global, with Benchmark, New Enterprise Associates, Redpoint Ventures, Icon Ventures and Two Sigma Ventures participating, valuing it at over $1 billion and bringing total funding to more than $180 million. It reported over 500 paying customers at the time. Today its site lists customers such as Polymarket and Linktree.

Tiger Cloud is priced by usage, with a 30-day free trial; prices are below. This profile draws on Tiger Data's own pages and published reporting. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

profile.platform: Cloud (AWS, Azure), self-managed and open source
profile.starts_at: Tiger Cloud compute from $30/month; 30-day free trial
profile.summary_short: TimescaleDB open-source time-series Postgres extension and the managed Tiger Cloud

gallery.alt: Tiger Data logo, a black tiger-head roundel with the words Tiger Data, Creators of TimescaleDB, on a yellow-green gradient
Illustration of a rising line chart on a yellow grid with the Tiger Data tiger-head logo in the middle, from the company's Year of the Tiger funding post

use_cases: Storing and querying metrics, IoT sensor data and events in PostgreSQL
Running real-time analytics dashboards on time-stamped data
Tracking financial and crypto price history
Compressing large time-series tables to cut storage costs
Combining vector and keyword search with relational data in Postgres

fit: already use PostgreSQL and need it to handle large time-series workloads
collect machine, IoT or observability data at scale
want an open-source core with the option of a managed cloud
not_fit: need a non-SQL document or key-value store
have small datasets that plain Postgres already handles well

pricing.intro: Tiger Cloud is priced by compute and storage, with a 30-day free trial. The figures below are from the official pricing page; storage prices are stated on the page as an effective price based on 5x compression.

plans.name: Performance
plans.detail: Storage $0.177/GB-month effective; up to 4 database services, 8 CPU and 32 GB memory per service

plans.name: Scale
plans.detail: Storage $0.212/GB-month effective; unlimited services, read replicas, tiered storage, private networking

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Up to 64 CPU and 256 GB memory per service, advanced security

notes: TimescaleDB itself remains open source and free to self-host.
Available on AWS and Azure, per the pricing page.

pros: Plain SQL and the full PostgreSQL ecosystem
cons: Name change from Timescale to Tiger Data may confuse search and docs
Cloud costs grow with compute and storage

alternatives.intro: Other databases for time-series and analytics. We have not compared them hands-on.

items.name: ClickHouse
items.difference: Column store aimed at analytics rather than a Postgres extension.

items.name: QuestDB
items.difference: Its own engine with SQL support, not Postgres.

faq.q: Is Timescale the same as Tiger Data?
faq.a: Yes. The company renamed itself Tiger Data in 2025. The open-source extension is still called TimescaleDB.
TimescaleDB remains open source. The managed Tiger Cloud is paid, with a 30-day free trial.

faq.q: How much does Tiger Cloud cost?
faq.a: Compute starts at $30 a month on the Performance plan and $36 on Scale, plus storage, according to the official pricing page.
